examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14074064/assets/243212bee1e50c7ca289142dcc8a9b5ac4f6d06fe3715661e99ec2601c82bf45.png)
Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a transformed system with the solution 

$$
X_1(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{ x_1(t) \right\} = \dfrac{4}{s} + \dfrac{1}{s-6}, 
\qquad
X_2(s) = \mathcal{L}\left\{ x_2(t) \right\} = \dfrac{20}{s} - \dfrac{1}{s-6}.
$$

Find the solution to the original initial value problem.
examples.worked_solution:
To find $x_1(t)$ and $x_2(t)$ satisfying the original initial value problem, we apply the inverse Laplace transform to $X_1(s)$ and $X_2(s){:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{1}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{4}{s}+\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}+{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =4\cdot 1+{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =4+{e}^{6t} \\ {x}_{2}(t) & ={L}^{-1}{{X}_{2}(s)} \\  & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{20}{s}-\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =20{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-6}} \\  & =20\cdot 1-{e}^{6\cdot t} \\  & =20-{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4+{e}^{6t} \\ 20-{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 20\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{e}^{6t}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=4{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=$ {{field-1}},
$\,{X}_{2}(s)=$ {{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{4{x}_{1}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=4L{{x}_{1}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}+3L{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+2=4{X}_{1}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-5={X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
s{X}_{1}(s)+2=4{X}_{1}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{1}(s)=-\frac{2}{s-4}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s)$ gives

$$
s{X}_{2}(s)-5=(-\frac{2}{s-4})+3{X}_{2}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{5s-22}{(s-3)(s-4)}.
$$
